learn.title: True or False
learn.body: A comparison asks a question about two values and answers `True` or `False`. These are values of type `bool`. An `if` uses that answer to decide what to do.

learn.title: Comparison operators
learn.body: It prints True, False, True, True. `==` asks if two values are equal, `!=` asks if they differ, and `<=` means less than or equal.

learn.title: = versus ==
learn.body: One `=` stores a value: `x = 5`. Two `==` compare: `x == 5` is `True` or `False`. Writing `if x = 5:` is an error. Mixing the two up is a very common beginner mistake.

learn.title: and, or, not
learn.body: It prints True, True, False. `and` needs both sides true, `or` needs at least one, and `not` flips the answer.
learn.code:
age = 15
has_ticket = True
print(age >= 12 and has_ticket)
print(age > 18 or has_ticket)
print(not has_ticket)

learn.title: Can they ride?
learn.body: Riders must be at least 120 cm tall and at least 8 years old. A child is 130 cm tall and 7 years old.
steps: True `and` False is False, so the child cannot ride

learn.body: Text can be compared too. `"cat" == "cat"` is True, but `"Cat" == "cat"` is False because case matters.

questions.explanation: 10 is equal to 10, so "not equal" is False.
`==` compares and gives True or False. `=` stores.
`3 > 2` is True but `2 > 5` is False. `and` needs both, so it is False.
`4 < 2` is False, and `not` flips it to True.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Each symbol asks a different yes or no question.

questions.prompt: To check that BOTH conditions are true, join them with \_\_.
questions.explanation: `and` is true only when both sides are true.
